earnings_release.text: EX-99.1 2 a2026-10x228xkex991earning.htm EX-99.1 Document Exhibit 99.1 Union Pacific Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results • Diluted EPS of $3.49, up 16%, and adjusted diluted EPS* of $3.53, up 15% • Operating ratio (OR) of 59.1% and adjusted OR* of 58.8% • Revenue carloads grew 6% Omaha, Neb., October 22, 2026 – Union Pacific Corporation (NYSE: UNP) today reported third quarter 2026 net income of $2.1 billion, up 16%, and diluted earnings per share (EPS) of $3.49, up 16%, compared to reported third quarter 2025 net income of $1.8 billion and diluted EPS of $3.01. Adjusted third quarter 2026 net income* of $2.1 billion increased 15%, and adjusted diluted EPS* of $3.53 increased 15%, compared to adjusted third quarter 2025 net income* of $1.8 billion and adjusted diluted EPS* of $3.08. "Union Pacific's third quarter results demonstrate our ability to safely deliver the service we sold to our customers while efficiently handling six percent volume growth," said Jim Vena, Union Pacific Chief Executive Officer. "We executed at a consistently high level, enabling record financial results and further reinforcing our position as the industry leader. We look forward to the upcoming steps of the Surface Transportation Board's merger review process and to delivering the benefits of America's first transcontinental railroad for our customers." Third Quarter Summary: 2026 vs. 2025 Financial Results: Record Financial Results Driven by Volume Growth, Pricing Strength and Operational Execution; Record Freight Revenue, Freight Revenue excluding Fuel Surcharge, Operating Revenue, Operating Income, and Net Income • Operating revenue of $7.2 billion grew 15% driven by higher fuel surcharge, 6% volume growth, core pricing gains and increased other revenue partially offset by business mix. • Freight revenue excluding fuel surcharge increased 6%. • Reported operating ratio improved 10 basis points to 59.1%. Adjusted operating ratio* increased 30 basis points to 58.8%. Higher fuel price unfavorably impacted operating ratio 140 basis points. Operating Results: Operational Excellence Supports Volume Growth; Record Workforce Productivity, Train Length, and Fuel Consumption Rate • Reportable personal injury rate improved. • Freight car velocity was 228 daily miles per car, a 1% increase. • Average terminal dwell was 19.9 hours, a 2% improvement. • Fuel consumption rate was 1.034, measured in gallons of fuel per thousand gross ton-miles, a 2% improvement. • Workforce productivity was 1,219 car miles per employee, a 5% increase. * See attached supplemental schedule of non-GAAP measures for a reconciliation to GAAP. -more- 2026 Outlook - On Track with Investor Day Targets Affirmed: • Meeting increased customer demand with strong service; mixed economic forecast. • Reported earnings per share growth of high-single digit; consistent with attaining 3-year CAGR target of high-single to low-double digit through 2027. • Pricing dollars in excess of inflation dollars. • Industry-leading operating ratio and return on invested capital. • Continued strong cash generation and consistent annual dividend increases. Updated: • Operating ratio improvement from core business; reported operating ratio challenged by high fuel prices. • Capital plan of $3.5 billion . Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Conference Call Union Pacific will webcast its third quarter 2026 earnings release presentation live at www.up.com/investor and via teleconference on Thursday, October 22, 2026, at 8:45 a.m. Eastern Time. Participants may join the conference call by dialing 877-407-8293 (or for international participants, 201-689-8349). ABOUT UNION PACIFIC Union Pacific (NYSE: UNP) delivers the goods families and businesses use every day with safe, reliable, and efficient service. Operating in 23 western states, the company connects its customers and communities to the global economy. Trains are the most environmentally responsible way to move freight, helping Union Pacific protect future generations. More information about Union Pacific is available at www.up.com.
